narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: a patient, precise instructor who counts out loud, demonstrates from the front and the back, repeats every step slowly three times before speeding up, names mistakes kindly and never rushes
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

episode_1.title: Meet American Tribal Style Belly Dance

scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Language of the Tribe
This is American Tribal Style Belly Dance. Late 20th century.
on_screen: Hero video, first 10 seconds (_DTMoZf1jis)
Title card: American Tribal Style Belly Dance · United States · Late 20th century

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The style originated in California in the late 1960s and 1970s with Jamila Salimpour’s Bal Anat, which presented a folkloric-inspired aesthetic.
Masha Archer later refined the 'tribal' group dynamic.
Carolena Nericcio-Bohlman formalized the current ATS format in 1987 through FatChanceBellyDance, creating the standardized cueing system.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: ATS is performed at community events, festivals, and parades.
It emphasizes group cohesion and mutual support rather than individual competition.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Fat Chance Belly Dance Live (https://archive.org/details/fat-chance-belly-dance-live-199-dance-vhs_1)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers operate in a group (tribe) using a standardized vocabulary of movements.
The leader is positioned at the far left.
Dancers use physical cues to signal transitions between movements.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (_DTMoZf1jis)
Signature moves — MISSING
Formation: Leader is always farthest to the left, followers to the right. Dancers angle their bodies to the left to read cues.
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Music is drawn from North Africa, the Middle East, India, and Eastern Europe, often fused with modern elements.
Dancers play zils (finger cymbals) during fast movements, using patterns like the 'military' (3-3-7) or 'Moroccan 6'.
Listen for the Zils (finger cymbals).
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Costumes feature tiered skirts (10-25 meters), cholis, coin bras, and heavy oxidized silver jewelry.
Hair is often worn up with flowers or hair gardens.
Makeup is eye-focused with heavy kohl or kajal.
on_screen: Images — MISSING
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Jamila Salimpour, Masha Archer, Carolena Nericcio-Bohlman, Paulette Rees-Denis, Kajira Djoumahna.
Variants include Gypsy Caravan, BlackSheep Bellydance, Unmata, Saada, and Datura, which often explore fusion elements.
Descended from Jamila Salimpour's Bal Anat, through Masha Archer's San Francisco Classic Dance Company, to Carolena Nericcio-Bohlman's FatChanceBellyDance.

music_brief.purpose: original soundtrack faithful to the tradition, with documented commercial reuse rights and no recurring royalties
music_brief.rights_rule: A composition brief does not clear an output. Record the provider/model/version, terms and date, input rights, output licence, restrictions and review before release.
music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of American Tribal Style Belly Dance (United States). Rhythm pattern: Military (3-3-7) or Moroccan 6. Instruments: Zils (finger cymbals). Mood: ancient, connected, vibrant. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

tracks.use: chapters: dance it to the music

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
